target_segment: SMB and mid-market ecommerce sellers; widely used by accounting/bookkeeping firms serving these clients
target_vertical: Multi-channel ecommerce retailers and DTC brands (Amazon FBA/FBM, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, Walmart, BigCommerce). Not a manufacturing tool; positioned as the ecommerce accounting-reconciliation layer.
pricing_model: Tiered subscription based on (a) number of sales channels connected and (b) monthly order volume per channel. Per-channel pricing on Standard plans; Multi-Channel plans bundle several channels at a lower combined rate.
starting_price_usd: USD $19/month (Mini tier, single channel, up to ~200 orders/month); commonly cited entry at $29/month for the next tier. Top Premium/Multi-Channel plans reach ~$899/month (5 channels, up to 100,000 combined orders).
free_trial_or_freemium: Free trial available (free to install on Shopify App Store; typical 30-day free trial across channel apps). No permanent free tier.
shopify_install_count: ~3,061 reviews on the Shopify App Store; A2X publicly cites 12,000+ businesses across all channels
shopify_sync_direction: One-way: Shopify -> A2X -> accounting ledger. A2X reads payouts/orders/fees from Shopify and posts summary journals/invoices to Xero/QBO/Sage/NetSuite. Does not push inventory, products, or fulfillment back to Shopify.
shopify_synced_entities: Payouts (Shopify Payments and third-party gateways), orders (as summaries, not per-order invoices by default), sales, refunds, fees, gift cards, shipping, taxes, discounts, tips, adjustments. COGS journals (when enabled). Shopify B2B orders synced as individual B2B invoices in addition to grouped settlement.
shopify_service_item_support: not applicable - A2X does not maintain an item master or differentiate service vs physical SKUs; all revenue flows through mapped ledger accounts at the settlement-summary level.
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes - multiple Shopify stores can be connected, each as a separate A2X account/channel (additional subscription cost per store).
shopify_pos_support: Yes - Shopify POS transactions are included in the Shopify payout summaries A2X reconciles; A2X publishes guidance on reconciling Shopify POS accounting.
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: Yes - dedicated A2X for Shopify B2B handling: B2B orders flagged in Shopify sync as individual B2B invoices to the ledger (debit A/R, credit configured B2B revenue account), in addition to being part of the grouped Shopify settlement.
shopify_markets_support: Yes - A2X for Shopify Markets Pro support since Dec 2023, automatically generating a payout for the net Markets Pro bank deposit including order revenue, fees, and charges.
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: not applicable - A2X does not map per-item metafields; mappings are at the transaction-type level to GL accounts and tax codes.
shopify_variant_option_mapping: not applicable at the accounting-sync layer - A2X does not sync products/variants. SKU-level cost data is used only inside A2X's optional COGS module to value movements.
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Settlement/payout-driven (auto-post on payout). Effectively near-real-time once Shopify closes a payout; not per-order webhook posting by default.
shopify_known_limitations: Not an order-management or inventory tool: no per-order invoice (by design - summary journal is the differentiator); cannot create/update Shopify products or push fulfillments; complex tax mapping requires manual setup; multi-store and multi-channel sellers pay per channel which becomes expensive; finalizing bank reconciliation in Xero can lag when payouts cross month-end (A2X does split settlements that span months).
etsy_native_or_third_party: Direct Etsy API integration by A2X (not via Codisto or another marketplace partner)
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: Sync only - A2X does not create or edit Etsy listings; it consumes Etsy receipt and payout data for accounting only.
etsy_inventory_sync: not applicable - A2X does not sync inventory levels to/from Etsy. Optional COGS module values sold units against SKU-level cost in A2X.
etsy_order_import: Automatic - A2X pulls Etsy receipts/payouts on a scheduled basis and groups them into settlement summaries aligned to deposit periods.
etsy_synced_entities: Etsy payouts, sales, fees (listing, transaction, payment processing, regulatory operating fee, offsite ads, Etsy Plus), refunds, sales tax, shipping, discounts; COGS journal when enabled.
etsy_known_limitations: Pure accounting layer - no listing management, variation editing, personalization metadata, or digital-product handling beyond posting the revenue and fees to GL.
amazon_supported: Native (A2X for Amazon - the company's original product, launched 2014/2015)
amazon_marketplaces: All major Amazon Seller Central marketplaces: US, CA, MX, BR, UK, DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, SE, PL, BE, TR, AE, SA, EG, IN, JP, AU, SG. [uncertain] on exact 2026 list.
amazon_seller_types: FBA and FBM (Seller Central). Vendor Central support: [uncertain] - A2X is primarily marketed for Seller Central settlement reports.
amazon_synced_entities: Settlement reports (Amazon Seller Central): sales, refunds, FBA fees, referral fees, storage fees, advertising charges, reserves/pending balances, shipping, gift wrap, marketplace facilitator tax, promotional rebates, chargebacks, FBA reimbursements, lending repayments. COGS journals when enabled.
amazon_listing_creation: not applicable - A2X does not create or update Amazon listings.
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: not applicable - A2X does not manage FBA inbound shipments.
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: not applicable - A2X integrates with Amazon Reports/Finances APIs (settlement data), not the FBA Inbound API.
amazon_settlement_report_handling: Core competency. A2X automatically retrieves each Amazon settlement (typically biweekly), parses every line item by transaction type, and posts a single summary invoice (or bill, if the settlement is a net charge) per settlement to the connected ledger. Each line maps to user-configured GL accounts and tax codes. Settlements that span two months are split so each portion lands in the correct period. The posted invoice/bill total matches the Amazon deposit exactly, enabling one-click bank reconciliation in Xero/QBO.
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: Explicit handling. A2X separately identifies Marketplace Facilitator Tax (MFT) lines in the Amazon settlement (US states, EU/UK marketplace facilitator VAT, AU GST, etc.) and maps them, by default, to a sales-tax-liability account on the balance sheet so they do not inflate revenue or affect seller-side tax filings. Both the MFT collected and the corresponding MFT principal/withheld lines are netted against the same liability account.
amazon_multi_account_support: Yes - multiple Amazon seller accounts can be connected (typically as separate A2X subscriptions/channels).
amazon_known_limitations: Pure accounting layer - no inventory sync, no listing/repricing, no FBA inbound, no Buy Shipping. Some users report tricky initial tax-code mapping and that very high-volume sellers feel the per-channel pricing.
xero_supported: Native (A2X is a Xero connected app)
xero_app_store_certified: Listed and certified on the Xero App Store
xero_app_awards_recognition: Xero US Small Business App of the Year 2025; Xero UK Practice App of the Year 2024; 2025 finalist in Xero UK Practice App of the Year and Global People's Choice categories
xero_app_store_rating: ~4.97 average across 850+ reviews on the Xero App Store (US); consistently among the most-reviewed apps on the Xero App Store
xero_synced_entities: Invoices (one per settlement/payout summary), bills (when a settlement is a net charge, e.g. negative Amazon disbursement), payments (matched against the bank deposit), contacts (one per sales channel), COGS journal entries (non-cash, debit COGS / credit Inventory Asset, posted as a zero-total bill in Xero that the user must approve), inventory adjustment journals via the COGS module. Does not sync products/inventory items as Xero items.
xero_accounting_sync_mode: summary_journal (the canonical example of this pattern). One invoice per Amazon settlement / Shopify payout / Etsy/eBay/Walmart payout, grouping all sales, fees, taxes, refunds, and adjustments by transaction type. Shopify B2B is a hybrid exception: B2B orders also sync as individual invoices in addition to being part of the grouped settlement.
xero_cogs_journal_method: periodic_journal. A2X optionally posts a non-cash month-end (or settlement-period) journal: debit Cost of Goods Sold, credit Inventory Asset, valued from SKU-level costs maintained inside A2X (manual, CSV import, or some channel-supplied cost). It is not a perpetual per-movement valuation and does not produce landed-cost-inclusive entries in the Xero stock module.
xero_multi_currency: Yes - A2X imports settlement data in the channel/home currency and uses Xero's multi-currency engine for FX conversion to the base currency; multi-currency invoices and bills are supported where the Xero subscription allows.
xero_tracking_category_mapping: Yes, granular: tracking category can be applied at the overall invoice level, per transaction-type category (e.g. sales vs fees vs MFT), or per individual transaction line. Common uses: split by Amazon marketplace (US/UK/EU/AU), by sales channel, or by product class.
xero_tax_handling: Per-transaction-type and per-line tax-rate mapping in A2X (e.g. UK 20% VAT, US no-tax, Australian GST, MFT to sales-tax-liability). Supports country-specific marketplace facilitator VAT/GST treatment. Manual setup required to get tax codes right; this is one of the most common onboarding pain points cited in reviews.
xero_known_limitations: COGS journals post as zero-total Bills in Drafts that must be manually approved to commit (workflow quirk specific to Xero); no per-order invoices outside of Shopify B2B; cannot push items/products to Xero inventory; very high-volume sellers can hit Xero line/invoice size considerations on large settlements (A2X aggregates per type to mitigate).
qb_desktop_supported: No - QuickBooks Online only. [uncertain] for any limited Desktop support; not part of A2X's marketed integrations.
qb_app_certified: Listed on the Intuit QuickBooks App Store
qb_app_store_rating: [uncertain] specific Intuit App Store star rating - widely cited as ~4.9 across review aggregators (G2 4.9, Capterra 4.9)
qb_synced_entities: Invoices (per settlement summary), bills (for net-negative settlements), payments, customers (one per channel), COGS as month-end Journal Entries (one JE per month, source data attached), inventory-asset adjustments via the same JE.
qb_accounting_sync_mode: summary_journal (same pattern as Xero). One summary invoice per channel payout; Shopify B2B individual invoices as a hybrid exception.
qb_cogs_journal_method: periodic_journal. Monthly non-cash Journal Entry: debit COGS, credit Inventory Asset, valued from SKU costs maintained in A2X. Not perpetual per movement; not landed-cost inclusive.
qb_multi_currency: Yes - supports QBO multi-currency where the QBO subscription allows.
qb_class_location_mapping: Yes - A2X for QBO supports Class and Location mapping at invoice and transaction-type level, analogous to Xero tracking categories (e.g. one Class per Amazon marketplace).
qb_known_limitations: QBO-only; manual tax mapping; COGS is monthly periodic JE rather than per-order; no inventory item sync.
other_ecom_channels: Direct A2X-built integrations: eBay, Etsy, Walmart, BigCommerce, Amazon Pay (reconciles Amazon Pay payouts across Shopify/WooCommerce/BigCommerce/other storefronts), PayPal (settlement reconciliation). TikTok Shop, WooCommerce (native), Wix, Squarespace, Faire, Square, Magento are NOT directly supported by A2X as of 2026; sellers on those platforms typically use Link My Books or Bookkeep instead.
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: not applicable - A2X is not a stock/inventory engine; bundles/kits and component decomposition are out of scope. Only SKU-level COGS values can be set.
other_accounting_integrations: NetSuite (native A2X for NetSuite, targeted at larger/enterprise sellers), Sage Business Cloud Accounting (UK only; A2X does not integrate with Sage in US/Canada). Sage Intacct, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks, Wave: not supported.
landed_cost_support: Partial / not applicable - users can include landed-cost components in the unit cost they upload into A2X's COGS module, but A2X does not allocate freight/duty/insurance across receipts or maintain a perpetual landed-cost valuation.
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: not applicable - COGS module holds a single per-SKU cost value; no per-currency valuation.
ai_natural_language_query: [uncertain] - no widely advertised natural-language query feature as of May 2026
public_api: [uncertain] - A2X does not publicly market a developer REST API for third parties; integrations with Xero/QBO/Sage/NetSuite and channels are built and operated by A2X itself. A 'Become an Integration Partner' program exists for channel integrators.
webhook_event_coverage: [uncertain] - no public webhook catalog documented for external consumers
integration_architecture: Native point-to-point: A2X is itself the iPaaS-like middleware between a sales channel (Amazon SP-API, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, Walmart, BigCommerce) and an accounting ledger (Xero, QBO, Sage UK, NetSuite). Cloud-hosted SaaS; no Zapier/Celigo/MESA dependency. Architecture is explicitly settlement/payout driven: A2X waits for the channel to close a payout, retrieves the underlying report, transforms it into a summarized journal/invoice, and posts via the accounting platform's API.
zapier_make_support: [uncertain] - not a marketed integration path; A2X's value is the native channel-to-ledger pipeline, so Zapier/Make/n8n are not the documented route.
mobile_app: [uncertain] - A2X is primarily a web application; no notable native mobile app marketed as of May 2026.
rate_limit_handling_documented: [uncertain] - A2X manages channel and accounting API rate limits internally but does not publish a developer-facing throttle/retry contract.
sync_frequency: Channel payout/settlement driven. Amazon: per settlement (typically every 14 days). Shopify: per payout (1-3 day cadence depending on Shopify Payments schedule). Etsy/eBay/Walmart/BigCommerce: per payout. Auto-post on receipt of a closed settlement is supported. Not a real-time per-order webhook stream.
